case_title: Gaurav Maini v. State of Haryana
accused_victim_relationship: Acquaintance: victim knew accused Gaurav Bhalla from before; the other three accused were not known to the victim. Defence alleged a love affair between Gaurav Bhalla and the victim's sister.
weapon: Pistol and knife (alleged in the robbery); an air pistol was alleged to have been recovered
evidence_type: Oral testimony of the victim and father (identification), call detail records, alleged recoveries, Section 27 disclosures; investigating officer's testimony
confession: Alleged s.27 disclosure statements by accused; not relied on. Court held disclosure statements were not proved as per law.
aggravating_circumstances: Ransom of Rs. 1 crore demanded; threats to kill the victim and family; armed robbery of victim; victim confined and blindfolded
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.364A (life imprisonment, fine Rs. 10,000), s.392 (RI 5 years, fine Rs. 5,000), s.120B (life imprisonment, fine Rs. 10,000)
high_court_outcome: Appeals dismissed; conviction and sentences upheld
neutral_facts: On a day in early April, the victim, a minor boy, went out in his car to play badminton and did not return home that evening. Later that night, his family began receiving telephone calls from unknown callers claiming the boy was in their custody and demanding a ransom of one crore rupees, with threats to kill the boy and harm the family if the police were informed. The family gathered cash from various sources and, on instructions from the callers, left the money in a car at a hospital area and then went to another location. Shortly afterwards the boy was found standing in a market area and was brought home. According to the victim, three men had stopped his car on the way home from the playground, one holding a pistol. He was robbed of his watch, ATM card, identity card, gold chain and cash, blindfolded, and kept confined overnight in a room, where he heard the men calling each other by name. The family did not report the matter to police for about two weeks. Police acted on source information about a kidnapping gang and registered a case without a complaint from the family. The investigating officer traced two mobile numbers used for the ransom calls through the service provider and SIM sale records. Several men were arrested and disclosure statements were recorded, followed by alleged recoveries of cash, a motorcycle, watches, mobile phones, a car and an air pistol. The victim later identified the accused at a later stage of the proceedings, and call detail records were produced.
physical_harm: No injuries described; victim was confined overnight, blindfolded, and robbed at gunpoint and knifepoint
financial_property_loss: Ransom of Rs. 1 crore alleged paid; victim's wrist watch, ATM card, gold chain and cash alleged robbed
premeditation_planning: Not identified as accused's premeditation; Court found the investigating agency's conduct suspicious
motive: alleged: ransom of Rs. 1 crore (prosecution case); Court did not accept the prosecution story
key_evidence_accepted: None accepted as reliable. Court found call detail records inadmissible without s.65B proof, recoveries and disclosures unproved, and dock identification doubtful.
witness_credibility: Father (PW-1) and victim (PW-2) found to have inherent improbabilities going to the root of the case; victim's identification not free from doubt; victim omitted accused names in earlier statement
custody_duration: Accused A1: about 10 years 11 months; A2: about 9 years; A3: 7 years 2 months; A4: about 10 years 10 months (as stated at hearing)
bail_history: Appellants were on bail at the time of the Supreme Court judgment; earlier bail history not stated
trial_duration: offence: 2 April 2003; trial judgment: 26 September 2005; High Court: 19 January 2009; Supreme Court: 09 July 2024
legal_representation: For appellants: Ms. Kiran Suri and Neeraj Kumar Jain (Sr. Advs.) with others. For State: S. Udaya Kumar Sagar, A.A.G., with Ms. Bina Madhavan and Dr. Monika Gusain.
investigation_status: FIR registered 15 April 2003 (on source information); charge sheet filed against seven accused; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Currency notes returned without court order; no s.452 final disposal order; secret information not on record; special report omitted accused names; grandfather (Shamlal Garg) not examined; statements delayed; notes not sealed or deposited in malkhana
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted and sentenced. High Court: appeals dismissed, conviction upheld. Supreme Court: appeals allowed, accused acquitted.
prosecution_argument: Victim's testimony was unimpeachable and corroborated by father's testimony, the grandfather's statement and recoveries; s.106 and s.114(a) Evidence Act presumption applied to recovered articles; father's silence explained by threats
defence_argument: Case fabricated; family delayed reporting; grandfather's statement omitted accused's identity; recoveries unproved and currency notes returned without court order; no TIP; defence witnesses ignored; case cooked up over love affair
legal_principle_applied: Duty of trial court under s.311 CrPC read with s.165 Evidence Act to summon essential witnesses; adverse inference for non-examination of a vital witness; s.451/452/457 CrPC for disposal of case property; s.65B for electronic records; benefit of doubt through inherent improbabilities
precedent_relied_upon: Pooja Pal v. Union of India (2016) 3 SCC 135; Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal (2020) 3 SCC 216
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds discharged; pending applications disposed of; no compensation or other directions
